author: ojiudezue
title: Thermostat brands = code profiles, auto-detected, visible per zone; Generic is the safety net
summary: Each brand family is a code profile (capabilities, hold method, person-change detection, timings) in the hvac_strategy registry, matched from the device registry (integration + manufacturer, then integration, then Generic) and shown as 'Thermostat type: … — detected' in Zone HVAC with an override. No user-defined manufacturer UI or research DB. Generic = setpoint-only holds, change detection vs URA's last write, no borrows until proven. First non-Carrier target: ecobee over HomeKit in the second home (no climate presets; Home/Sleep/Away is a select; Clear Hold button).
why: What differs between brands is behaviour (how a hold looks, how a person's change shows), which needs code and tests; a form could only hold numbers and a wrong entry would make URA fight the thermostat. The second home goes live the weekend of 2026-10-03 with an ecobee.
implications: Second home runs with the HVAC coordinator OFF until the ecobee profile is validated there (its URA v5.103.18 has HVAC enabled with no zones — must be switched off before zones are added). Phases: P1 route every write through the profile, Carrier byte-identical; P2 detection + zone setting + Generic hardening; P3 ecobee profile against the real install.
revisit_trigger: A third brand appears, or the ecobee needs behaviour a profile can't express.
